query: What customer issues create the most support burden?

per_column.name: customer_urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Urgency/priority reflects how the customer perceives the issue and drives prioritization, but it is not itself a constitutive part of the operational burden (the effort/load on support). It predicts burden rather than being an aspect of it.

per_column.name: system_criticality
per_column.rationale: Describes the nature/criticality of the affected system, an attribute of the issue that influences burden, not a part of the burden itself. Values also mix issue types (feature_request, payment) blurring the meaning.

per_column.name: user_impact_scale
per_column.rationale: The breadth of user impact (single_user to entire_tenant) is a genuine dimension of the burden's magnitude -- the scope of what must be handled is an aspect of the operational load.

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Classifies the type of issue causing burden; it is an attribute of the driver, not a constitutive aspect of the burden itself.

per_column.name: blocking_or_workaround_status
per_column.rationale: Whether the issue is fully blocking vs. has a workaround captures the severity/impact dimension of the burden -- an aspect of how heavy the load is.

per_column.name: escalation_requirement
per_column.rationale: The level and type of escalation needed (platform engineering, p1 bridge, etc.) is a constitutive part of the operational effort/coordination burden.

per_column.name: remediation_type
per_column.rationale: The kind of remediation work required (hotfix, data recovery, documentation) is a direct component of the operational work performed to resolve the issue.

judge.rationale: Operational_burden (the workload/effort imposed on support) is only partially decomposed into true meronymic facets. Genuine parts of the burden are its impact scale, severity/blocking status, escalation/coordination requirement, and remediation work type. However, several columns are external predictors or descriptors of the issue rather than constitutive parts: customer_urgency_signal (customer perception/priority), system_criticality (system attribute), and issue_category (type of issue). Mutual exclusivity is weakened by overlap: system_criticality, issue_category, remediation_type, and blocking_or_workaround_status share the same underlying issue-type/severity signal (e.g., feature_request, configuration, production outage recur across columns), so multiple columns re-encode the same aspect. Exhaustiveness is moderate: the effort/time dimension itself (e.g., handling time, number of touches, recurrence/volume) -- arguably the core of 'burden' -- is not captured by any facet, and resolution_minutes already in the original table is the closest proxy. Overall this is a mixed set with meaningful facets diluted by predictors and redundancy.
